content: Doris K. Miller, often known as Dorie Miller, was an African American Navy mess attendant who became famous for his heroic actions during the Pearl Harbor attack on December 7, 1941. Despite being assigned to non-combat duties due to racial segregation in the military at the time, Miller manned an anti-aircraft gun and fired at Japanese planes during the attack, helping to defend the USS West Virginia. He was the first African American to be awarded the Navy Cross for his bravery. Miller was killed in action in 1943 when his ship was sunk during World War II. His heroism helped raise awareness about racial inequality in the U.S. military and contributed to discussions about integration.
